open_questions.q: Which repeating list — schedule_k_items (distributive shares to K-1) vs deduction_line_items vs balance-sheet lines
open_questions.recommendation: schedule_k_items, since partner qualifying income derives from Schedule K; revisit if a rule reads deductions or the balance sheet GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Partner-level attribution — the borrower's usable income is their ownership share; confirm whether the matching K-1 supplies the share or this transcript must carry per-partner detail
open_questions.recommendation: confirm with the rule author whether per-partner detail is needed on this transcript GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): the matching K-1 supplies the partner's share; no per-partner detail on this transcript.

notes: Serves 0 rules — no rule in the packet names this document; fields justified by identity, PII, and processor use. The business-return chain feeds self-employment income analysis (IN-12) but no rule is attached in the packet.

17 typed-core rows. No rule floor; the income chain (receipts -> COGS -> gross profit -> total income -> ordinary business income) plus guaranteed payments are the figures a self-employment calculation would read; identity/EIN attach the return to the borrower's ownership.

Form 1065 is a partnership informational return — income passes through to partners on Schedule K-1; the borrower's usable income is their K-1 share plus guaranteed payments, not the whole partnership total.
PII registry note: ein_masked pre_masked true; an existing employer_ein (masked) covers the same concept under a different name — reconcile naming rather than duplicate.
